projects_meta_description: Setlist, Fennevia, and Dial Canvas: three public software projects built and maintained by Ting.
projects_intro: Setlist and Fennevia are my two main projects: a public music-search service and a modular four-edge shell for stock Firefox. Dial Canvas is the smaller Firefox-first experiment alongside them. All three are public and still evolving.
project_setlist_description: Setlist is a self-hosted search index for VTuber karaoke. It finds public YouTube archives, extracts timestamped song lists from comments, and links each result to the start of the performance.
project_setlist_feature_search: Fast song search with channel, content type, and date filters
project_setlist_feature_links: Timestamp-aware YouTube links to each performance
project_setlist_feature_languages: English, Traditional Chinese, and Japanese interface
project_tech_intro: Setlist crosses the whole stack: search UI, ingestion workers, a relational data model, and a deployment I operate on my own infrastructure.
project_fennevia_alt: Fennevia Browse Your Way brand artwork showing a modular four-edge browser shell and widget placement guides
project_fennevia_feature_edges: Drag nearly every visible control between four edge panels and compose nested Row and Column layouts
project_fennevia_feature_native: Tabs, bookmarks, downloads, and the address launcher adapt to horizontal or vertical placement
project_fennevia_feature_recovery: A validated bridge keeps security-sensitive flows in Firefox and fails open to the retained native interface
project_dial_alt: Stylized Dial Canvas new-tab layout with movable dials and widgets
project_dial_feature_canvas: Free-form dials can be moved, resized, grouped across pages, and arranged without a fixed grid
project_dial_feature_widgets: Clock, weather, notes, tasks, calendar, holidays, and wallpaper information widgets
project_dial_feature_storage: Local by default, with optional Firefox Sync when you choose to turn it on
projects_more_heading: I build the part people touch and the part that has to survive.
projects_more_body: The shape changes from project to project, but the test is the same: the interface should feel clear, the system should be recoverable, and the maintenance should still make sense six months later.

profile_hero_title_line_1: I build software people can use—
profile_hero_title_line_2: and the systems that keep it running.
profile_hero_intro: Hi, I'm Ting, a software engineer and system architect in Hong Kong. I move between product code, infrastructure, automation, and the occasional AI experiment that earns its keep.
profile_now_body: Keeping Setlist healthy, testing Fennevia against new Firefox builds, and making Dial Canvas easier to shape by hand.
profile_work_heading: Two main projects, plus one smaller browser experiment.
profile_work_intro: Setlist turns scattered music data into a public service. Fennevia makes Firefox chrome modular. Dial Canvas explores a freer new-tab layout. All three are public.
project_setlist_alt: Setlist search interface showing VTuber karaoke song results
project_fennevia_description: Fennevia is an experimental, content-first interface for stock Firefox. It turns browser chrome into a modular four-edge workspace where nearly every visible control can be moved, nested, or reoriented. A narrow, validated bridge leaves security-sensitive flows with Firefox and can fall back to the retained native interface. The Windows prerelease tracks current Firefox Release builds and is intended for a dedicated profile.
project_dial_description: A free-form speed-dial canvas for the new tab page. Dials and widgets can be moved, resized, and arranged without a rigid grid. Data stays local unless optional Firefox Sync is turned on.
profile_intro: I work on software, infrastructure, automation, and self-hosted systems. My projects often involve both the underlying platform and the software that runs on it.
profile_currently_body: I currently run a Proxmox VE homelab, research AI, LLMs, and agents, test locally deployed models, and build small tools to reduce repetitive work.
profile_about_heading: I like projects that cross the line between product and infrastructure.
profile_about_p1: I'm a software engineer in Hong Kong. The work I enjoy most starts with a real annoyance, then follows it all the way from the interface to deployment and maintenance.
profile_about_p2: My homelab is where I try those ideas under real conditions. It runs on Proxmox VE, with network segmentation, containers, reverse proxies, and enough automation that routine work stays routine.
profile_about_p3: I also experiment with LLMs and agents, but I keep the boundary obvious: they can help with work; they do not get to make opaque operational decisions on their own.
profile_focus_platform_desc: Clear boundaries, useful logs, tested recovery, and fewer surprises beat clever infrastructure.
profile_focus_product_desc: I care about the handoff between the UI, API, data, and the way the thing is actually shipped.
profile_focus_ai_desc: I use local and cloud models where the result can be reviewed, measured, and safely corrected.
profile_portfolio_heading: Setlist is my first public homelab service.
profile_portfolio_body: It combines a search interface, a reliable data pipeline, and a secure self-hosted deployment.
